solution:
Curl test: $\partial F_y/\partial x = 8x = \partial F_x/\partial y$, so a potential exists.

$U = -\int F_x\,dx = -(4x^2y - 3x) + g(y)$, and $-\partial U/\partial y = 4x^2 - g'(y)$ must equal $F_y = 4x^2$, so $g$ is a constant (take 0).

$W = -\Delta U = U(0, 0) - U(3, 4) = 0 - (-135) =$ **135 J**.

Curl test: $\partial F_y/\partial x = 8x = \partial F_x/\partial y$, so a potential exists.

$U = -\int F_x\,dx = -(4x^2y - 5x) + g(y)$, and $-\partial U/\partial y = 4x^2 - g'(y)$ must equal $F_y = 4x^2$, so $g$ is a constant (take 0).

$W = -\Delta U = U(0, 0) - U(1, 1) = 0 - (1) =$ **-1 J**.

$U = -\int F_x\,dx = -(x^2y - 5x) + g(y)$, and $-\partial U/\partial y = x^2 - g'(y)$ must equal $F_y = x^2$, so $g$ is a constant (take 0).

$W = -\Delta U = U(0, 0) - U(1, -3) = 0 - (8) =$ **-8 J**.

Curl test: $\partial F_y/\partial x = 6x = \partial F_x/\partial y$, so a potential exists.

$U = -\int F_x\,dx = -(3x^2y + 6x) + g(y)$, and $-\partial U/\partial y = 3x^2 - g'(y)$ must equal $F_y = 3x^2$, so $g$ is a constant (take 0).

$W = -\Delta U = U(0, 0) - U(4, 2) = 0 - (-120) =$ **120 J**.

prompt: A rocket of total mass 330 t (1 t = 1000 kg) rises vertically. Propellant making up 80% of the mass burns at a steady 1400 kg/s, with exhaust speed 3000 m/s relative to the rocket. Ignoring drag and using $g = 9.8$ m/s² throughout, find the thrust (N), the acceleration at liftoff (m/s²) and the speed at burnout (m/s), each to 3 significant figures.
solution:
Thrust: $uR = (3000)(1400) = 4.2 \times 10^{6}$ N, that is **4200000 N**.

Liftoff: $a = \dfrac{uR}{m_i} - g = \dfrac{4.2 \times 10^{6}}{3.3 \times 10^{5}} - 9.8 =$ **2.93 m/s²**.

Burn time: $t_b = \dfrac{0.80\times330000\text{ kg}}{1400\text{ kg/s}} = 189$ s, and $m_i/m_f = 1/(1 - 80/100)$.

Burnout: $v = u\ln\dfrac{m_i}{m_f} - gt_b = 3000\ln\dfrac{1}{1 - 80/100} - 9.8(189) =$ **2980 m/s** (gravity loss 1850 m/s).

The gravel arrives with no horizontal velocity, so its relative velocity is $-v$ and $0 = F - vR$: $F = Rv = 30(3.5) =$ **105 N**.

Power: $P = Fv = Rv^2 =$ **368 W**.

The gravel gains kinetic energy at $\tfrac12Rv^2$; the other half becomes heat: **184 W**.

The gravel arrives with no horizontal velocity, so its relative velocity is $-v$ and $0 = F - vR$: $F = Rv = 30(1) =$ **30 N**.

Power: $P = Fv = Rv^2 =$ **30 W**.

The gravel gains kinetic energy at $\tfrac12Rv^2$; the other half becomes heat: **15 W**.

Area: $A = \pi(5/200\text{ m})^2 = 0.00196$ m².

Mass flow rate: $\rho Av = 1000(0.00196)(29) =$ **56.9 kg/s**.

The wall removes all the forward momentum, so $F = \rho Av^2 = (56.9)(29) =$ **1650 N**.

Area: $A = \pi(2.5/200\text{ m})^2 = 0.000491$ m².

Mass flow rate: $\rho Av = 1000(0.000491)(27) =$ **13.3 kg/s**.

The wall removes all the forward momentum, so $F = \rho Av^2 = (13.3)(27) =$ **358 N**.

$v_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{5(8)}{5 + 6.5} = 3.478$ m/s and $\mu = \dfrac{(5)(6.5)}{5 + 6.5} = 2.826$ kg.

Relative kinetic energy: $\tfrac12\mu v_{\text{rel}}^2 = \tfrac12(2.826)(8)^2 = 90.4$ J. Lost: $(1 - 0.8^2)(90.4) =$ **32.6 J**.

In the CM frame the carts move at $8 - 3.478$ and $-3.478$ m/s; the collision reverses both and multiplies them by 0.8. Adding $v_{\text{cm}}$ back: $v_{1f} = v_{\text{cm}} - 0.8(v_1 - v_{\text{cm}}) =$ **-0.14 m/s** and $v_{2f} = (1 + 0.8)v_{\text{cm}} =$ **6.26 m/s**.
